2. Business Attire: Men should wear a suit and tie, and women should dress conservatively and business-like. Avoid revealing clothing and bright colors.

3. Meeting Etiquette: Be punctual and arrive early for meetings. Always wait for the other person to sit before sitting yourself. When addressing someone, use their title and last name.

4. Gift Giving: Gifts are not expected when doing business in Japan, but it is always appreciated. Make sure the gift is of good quality, and is wrapped neatly.

5. Business Cards: Make sure your business card is translated into Japanese, and always present your card with both hands.

6. Meeting Conclusion: End meetings on time, and make sure to follow up with any agreements or tasks that were discussed.

It is important to remember that business etiquette can vary between different companies and industries, so always do your research and follow the rules set by the company you are doing business with.</s>
